You ruined the whole wedding with a funeral.
Let us drink to our optimism.
Viktor Petrovich is in a coma.
His condition is stable but serious.
Vitya, forgive me, please.
That inspector was not real.

lines.trans: I staged all of this myself.
Who could have known it would turn out like this.
Please get well soon, Vitya.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'Lord', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Lord, why are you punishing me?
Good Lord, what happened?
Oh, Lord!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Thank you for the kind words.
What kind of total nonsense is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of total nonsense is this?
Now we will think of something, Chef.
Timur, what have you done here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
I am inspecting your restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you punish'.

examples.trans: What are you punishing me for?
Lord, why are you punishing me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Open up, he will freeze in there.
No, he did not come in here.
There are no other people inside there.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'breathing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: No breathing, we are starting resuscitation.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть дыхание.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always breathing.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'begin', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: No breathing, we are starting resuscitation.
When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'resuscitation' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: No breathing, we are starting resuscitation.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть реанимация.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always resuscitation.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Hello, I am very pleased to meet you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!
We do not wish you any harm.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'again', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our Lyova jammed up again.
It's another trick.
Rain again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'клинить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'jammed'.

examples.trans: Chef, our Lyova jammed up.
Our Lyova jammed up again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
Why did you do that just now?
How foolish you are!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'man' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Fedya, escort the man, please.
Because of me a person died today.
A human would not have been able to work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'entire', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He hanged himself out of jealousy.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вадьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'wedding' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And what about our wedding?
In the hall, it is her wedding.
What wedding today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ruined', paired with 'портить'.

examples.trans: You ruined the whole wedding with a funeral.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.
The rain spoiled our walk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хороны'). Common masculine noun meaning 'with a funeral' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You ruined the whole wedding with a funeral.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть похороны.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always with a funeral.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Let us make a bet then.
Let us test it right now!
Enough, let us sort this out calmly.

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let's drink', paired with 'выпивать'.

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
Drink some water.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And what about our wedding?
Let us drink to our optimism.
I love our town.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'optimism' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let us drink to our optimism.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть оптимизм.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always optimism.

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ходиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is located', paired with 'найтись'.

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?
The town is situated on a river.
Where is the operating room located here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Is everything alright with you?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'coma' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Yes, just do not tell anyone.
I will not tell anyone!
We will definitely not tell anyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Of course, you are completely free.
What kind of report will he write now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'остояние'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'state' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: His condition is stable but serious.
Checking the condition of the wall.
In good condition.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'табильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: His condition is stable but serious.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно стабильно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite stably and calmly.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('heavy; hard, difficult').

examples.trans: His condition is stable but serious.

examples.text: Я вообще в школе тяжёлый металл любила!
examples.trans: In school I actually loved heavy metal!
I had a heavy bag.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Lena, forgive me for everything.
Forgive me for hiding it from you.
Vitya, forgive me, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, please.
Please do not kill me.
Let me go from here, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
What kind of total nonsense is this?
Chef, those were just coconuts.

meanings.note: From Latin 'inspector' (observer, overseer, from 'inspicere', to look into).

examples.trans: I am inspecting your restaurant.
A Michelin inspector has come to see you.
I am inspecting your restaurant today.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Yes, it is just so unexpected.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, true').

examples.trans: We are true keepers of secrets.
That inspector was not real.
This is real success!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
What kind of total nonsense is this?
Chef, those were just coconuts.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'myself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You hinted at it to me yourself.
There is actually no money at all.
He hanged himself out of jealousy.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Is everything alright with you?
We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!

meanings.en: to rig, frame, set up maliciously
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'строить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to set up, arrange maliciously', paired with 'подстраивать'.

examples.trans: I staged all of this myself.
Did you set all this up in advance?
The fraudsters engineered a trap for the businessman.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
Viktor Petrovich, maybe it will blow over?
Who is going to climb in after him now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A coconut has already fallen on me.
Well, I am completely alive.
Let us make a bet then.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'knew'.

examples.trans: Wait, how will I recognize him?
So all of this is completely untrue!
So I am just imagining all of this.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
Yes, it is just so unexpected.
I will not withstand such a blow?

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will work out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.trans: It will all work out!
He'll make a good doctor.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.trans: Soon they will bring us this money.
I promised that I would quit soon.
Let us run upstairs quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'правляться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to gain weight; to recover', paired with 'поправиться'.

examples.text: Знаете, Лев, я поправляюсь очень быстро.
examples.trans: You know, Lev, I gain weight very quickly.

examples.text: После болезни дедушка начал быстро поправляться.
examples.trans: After his illness Grandfather began to recover quickly.
